changes.before: Define Flags<T> so every property value becomes boolean. enabledTheme reads the theme flag.
changes.after: Keep the same property names, but make their values true or false.

before: A mapped type visits the property names of another type. In { [K in keyof T]: boolean }, keyof T supplies the keys, K names each key in turn, and boolean is the new value type. It creates a type description, not a runtime object.

Settings has theme and attempts. Flags<Settings> keeps those names but changes both value types to boolean. The object still must be written at runtime. enabledTheme takes that flags object and returns its theme boolean; the call below returns true. This example starts with required mutable properties; mapped types can preserve modifiers, which is not a runtime freeze.
Optional local practice: Add a third required Settings property and update the flags object.
after: A mapped type builds a type from another type's property names. In `[K in keyof T]`, keyof T supplies the keys and K stands for each key in turn. Writing boolean after the colon makes every new value true or false.
Settings has theme and attempts. Flags<Settings> keeps those names but gives both boolean values. This creates a type description; you still write the actual object.
Adding another required property to Settings means the flags object needs that name too. The mapped type follows the keys in Settings.
If a setting called volume originally holds a number, its flag still needs true or false. A numeric flag value such as 8 would cause a type error.
